sections.what_happened: (a) UPDATE to 1400-03: the Sabina Shoal incident is now characterized as the FIRST known US freedom-of-navigation operation in the South China Sea in over a year. (b) NEW: Taiwan Coast Guard reported a standoff with a Chinese Coast Guard vessel in restricted waters near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands. (c) NEW: Reuters reports Trump has not approved a proposed $14B arms package for Taiwan. (d) NEW context: 27 PLA aircraft (incl. H-6 bombers) in a joint combat-readiness patrol Oct 20; Schriver called Chinese coast guard patrols east of Taiwan 'highly destabilising'.
sections.what_verified: Reuters relays (BusinessWorld, Straits Times, Baird Maritime, EconoTimes, Times Now).
sections.what_disputed: US Navy declined immediate comment on the Charleston; Beijing's 'illegal intrusion' framing is contested under UNCLOS interpretations.
sections.why_matters: A FONOP and a freeze in the same day: the US Navy returns to the South China Sea for the first time in over a year, while Trump reportedly sits on the $14B Taiwan arms package. Taipei forums call the patrols 'highly destabilising'; Beijing's southern theatre says it tracked the Charleston. Three capitals, three readings of the same Tuesday.
sections.context: Background: South China Sea + Taiwan cluster: first known US FONOP in SCS in >1yr at Sabina Shoal; Pratas standoff; Trump holds $14B Taiwan arms package

totw_analysis: Our read: A FONOP and a freeze in the same day: the US Navy returns to the South China Sea for the first time in over a year, while Trump reportedly sits on the $14B Taiwan arms package. Taipei forums call the patrols 'highly destabilising'; Beijing's southern theatre says it tracked the Charleston. Three capitals, three readings of the same Tuesday. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Washington sails a warship through China's claimed waters for the first time in a year — then reportedly shelves $14B of arms for Taiwan. Provocation, or a signal with the price tag removed?
